scope: Actual bundled read-only source inventory, identities, lexical dependencies, bounded diagnostics and retained source/framework ownership. No assembly, foreign dialect build, browser or device acceptance claim.

results.name: Existing Forge example has exact lexical dependencies and a syntactic-only report
Analysis preserves source bytes, project history, assembler fields and emulator state
Unknown declaration needs review and each foreign declaration blocks a Forge compatibility claim
Declaration metadata is bounded inert text and rejects undeclared fields
The existing workspace validator owns schema, normalized paths and base64 validation
Per-file and inventory/configuration identities match independent SHA256 calculations
Inventory order does not alter identity, while configured entry and build profile do
Snapshot identity remains tied to the bytes captured before asynchronous hashing
Unavailable hashing refuses without claiming an unverifiable identity or changing state
BOM, CRLF, CR and quoted semicolons retain physical bytes and precise 1-based lines
Comments and quoted strings never become dependencies
Relative paths normalize within the workspace and remain case sensitive
Unsafe dependency paths are reported without host filesystem interpretation
Missing includes and binary insertions identify originating file and line
Expressions and binary offsets retain uncertain lexical evidence without evaluating it
Label-prefixed and bare foreign include spellings cannot masquerade as Forge preprocessor support
Conditional dependency uncertainty propagates through nested includes and binary targets
A separate unconditional path promotes shared files without making conditional edges certain
Macro definitions and invocations avoid false unsupported instructions while dependencies remain uncertain
Forge macros named like foreign include directives are not invented dependencies
Repetition blocks keep dependency reachability uncertain without expanding loop bodies
Include cycles are bounded findings rather than recursive source expansion
Workspace inventory and entry reachability remain distinct for unused assembly and host files
Assembly .mac files and explicitly included ambiguous headers are scanned
Opaque binary insertions and unreferenced host scripts are inventoried without decoding
Explicit assembly includes and non-Lua entries use source role rather than filename extension
Binary insertion does not traverse assembly-looking target dependencies
Invalid UTF8 and binary control bytes in assembly are refused without replacing raw bytes
Known foreign directives and anonymous/scoped operands are explicit; unknown symbols are not invented errors
Missing or host entries and CHR profile dependencies are reported separately
Per-line, total-line and diagnostic caps produce explicitly incomplete reports
Repeated dependencies are scanned once per file and stop at the edge cap
